title: Tool-call schema delta checks and rollout invariants for safe model swaps
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add deterministic compatibility checks and runtime invariants for function/tool-calls during model rollouts. This ticket implements a light-weight, production-safe mechanism that detects breaking changes to structured outputs and function-call contracts during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts and triggers automatic mitigation (pause, rollback, or routing to fallback). The goal is to prevent silent contract regressions when swapping model variants or upgrading model families.
background: We frequently deploy new model variants (quantized, kernel-optimized, or new checkpoints) and route traffic using canary/AB policies. Recent rollouts exposed subtle function-call differences (parameter renames, type changes, nested field removal) that caused downstream tool integrations to misbehave under load. Existing tooling captures post-deployment errors but lacks pre-flight, continuous compatibility checks that work with shadow traffic and low-latency rollouts.
goals: Detect schema-level breakages in function-call outputs during rollouts with <1s extra latency added to canary flow
Surface a deterministic diff (function-name, param-set, param-types) per request and aggregate counts for SRE/PM/Design
Support automatic rollback/hold when compatibility thresholds are exceeded, and allow safe manual override
Enable offline replay & graded shadowing so teams can validate model changes before increasing traffic
Integrate with Console dashboards and rollout API for visibility and one-click rollback
non_goals: Full semantic equivalence detection (we only provide heuristics/metrics for semantic drift, not full-proof semantic equivalence)
Replacing developer QA or human review for large schema migrations
Performing heavy-weight ML-based diffing during hot-path inference (must remain lightweight)
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can compute a normalized function-call
delta between baseline model and candidate for a single request and emit a compact diff event
Rollout controller consumes diff events and implements policies: hold, rollback, or continue
Console shows per-route compatibility metric: schema_mismatch_rate, required_field_loss, extra_field_insertion with 1-minute resolution
Shadow traffic pipeline can replay 1000 requests/minute for a given route and produce a pre-rollout compatibility report
Smoke tests exercising a function-call rename and parameter type change should trigger the policy and mark the candidate as failed
design_decisions: Use JSON Schema (subset) as canonical representation for structured outputs; runtime computes normalized representations for comparison
Compute three levels of diff: structural (presence/absence of fields), type-diff (type changes for a field), and semantic warnings (field renamed heuristics based on stable IDs)
Keep hot-path checks bounded: perform schema validation and delta packing in the inference worker; send compact telemetry (hashes + small stubs) to controller to avoid large payloads
For function-call compatibility, compare function name and parameter keys; if names differ, apply a configurable mapping table before triggering failures
Policy composition: allow multiple thresholds (per-route and global). Example: schema_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 3 consecutive 1-minute intervals => auto-hold
Expose an admin "dry-run" mode for policy changes where events are recorded but do not affect routing
implementation_steps: 1) Define canonical JSON Schema subset and canonicalization rules (sorting keys, trimming nulls, unify numeric types)
2) Add a lightweight schema validator to inference worker that validates the model-produced tool-call payload against the route schema
3) Implement function-call delta generator that emits compact diffs: {fn_name_delta,hits,missing_required,extra_noncritical,types_changed} as a small telemetry record
4) Extend rollout controller to ingest diffs, compute rolling windows, and enforce policies (hold/rollback/route-to-fallback)
5) Add shadow traffic pipeline hook that routes a copy of requests to candidate models and collects diffs without affecting live responses
6) Build Console widgets: per-route compatibility timeseries, top diffs, recent sample diffs with links to replay
7) Add e2e tests and offline replay harness that can run historical traces and generate a compatibility report
8) Add safety gate: when schema mismatch rate spikes, automatically route new requests to pinned fallback model if configured
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Offline analysis (week 1): run replay on 10k request trace for target routes, produce baseline diffs and a compatibility report
Phase 1 - Shadow (week 2): enable shadow traffic to candidate at 100% of sampled requests for 48h. Ensure telemetry volume and latency are OK
Phase 2 - Canary (week 3): route 1% of live traffic to candidate with schema checks enabled. Observe metrics for 24h
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp (week 4): increase to 5% then 20% with monitoring and automated hold thresholds configured
Phase 4 - Full rollout or rollback (week 5): if thresholds cleared, proceed; otherwise rollback and triage
rollback_conditions: function_name_mismatch_rate >= 0.05% and > 10 absolute mismatches in an hour
end-to-end error rate increase > 0.2% attributable to candidate model (correlated via traces)
manual emergency stop by on-call through Console or API
testing_plan: Unit: schema canonicalizer tests, delta generator tests with synthetic function-call payloads
Integration: start candidate runtime with schema checks on a staging cluster and exercise a mixture of happy/edge-case tool-calls
Load: shadow pipeline replay at 1k r/s to validate telemetry throughput and ensure diff aggregation scales
Chaos: simulate partial worker failures and ensure controller handles partial telemetry loss without false positives
Regression: add a test case that renames a non-required param; verify it is surfaced as a non-blocking warning unless flagged by route policy
operational_notes: Telemetry volume: compact diffs are capped at 1KB per event; aggregate counters are preferred in high-throughput paths
Backward compatibility: new schema fields must be allowed by default; removals require an explicit migration plan
Operator workflow: Console will provide a 1-click rollback and an exportable compatibility report for postmortems
Security: diffs must not include user PII; redact any string fields matching configured patterns before emitting
Access controls: only SRE/PM/owner roles can change auto-rollback thresholds
